title: evidence-cli run check and answer check

claims.text: evidence-cli reads a finished associate run from its export: it re-checks every fact against the saved results, counts them, writes reviewer flags beside the run, and, as a separately named result, says whether the run's answer matches recorded expected values; associate imports it for its own re-check

honesty_conditions.text: both commands exist and associate's suite passes importing them

claims.text: the grader that marks a run's answer right or wrong lives in evidence-cli (operator, 2026-11-18)

the answer check is a separately named result, never folded into the evidence counts or any completeness grade, and every output says which of the two it is; this keeps the build brief's distinction that a complete trail does not mean the work is correct (operator, 2026-11-18)
the answer check and the run check are two commands of one package, evidence check and evidence grade, not a separate tool

revisions.text: the answer check and the run check are two commands of one package, not a separate tool (operator question 2026-11-18, answered by the assistant's recommendation; reversible)

claims.text: associate imports evidence-cli as a first-party, zero-dependency package with a version floor (operator, 2026-11-18)
associate, which imports the re-check as a library and calls the answer check from its measurement runner; an operator or reviewer checking one export or many from the command line

honesty_conditions.text: associate's test suite passes using only names this spec lists as public

claims.instruction: The library surface is what associate imports; the commands are what a person runs.

claims.text: evidence-cli is the template scaffold with no domain code; the only re-check of an associate run lives inside associate, and nothing anywhere marks a run's answer right or wrong

honesty_conditions.text: git ls-files evidence at origin/main lists only scaffold modules

claims.text: evidence check reads one export or many and prints counts per run and summed, each disagreement with the harness's own counts, and reviewer flags, and writes the flags to a file beside the run without touching the run's files; evidence grade takes an answer text and a task's expected values and returns matches, does not match or cannot tell, citing the rule that decided; the same code is importable, and associate uses it in place of its own

honesty_conditions.text: both commands run on the committed fixture exports and their output is identical on a second run

claims.text: one place holds the check, so associate gets leaner and every consumer gets the same fixes; and it gives the planned comparison a grader that is not the harness under test

honesty_conditions.text: associate's groundwork spec names evidence-cli as its grader and re-check

claims.text: 100% of the shared matcher and hand-back vectors pass in evidence-cli; counts over the fixture exports equal a hand count; a second run prints a byte-identical report; every file in the export is byte-identical after both commands; and for every fixture task the recorded answer is graded as matching and a hand-written wrong answer as not matching

honesty_conditions.text: each of the five checks is a named test in the evidence-cli suite

claims.instruction: Vectors: associate/contract/matcher_vectors.json at the pinned associate commit.

claims.text: the matcher, the checker, the counts, the export loader and the run-result summary move from associate/accuracy into evidence-cli with their tests, keeping function names and results; the public names are listed in the documentation and a change to any of them is a breaking release

honesty_conditions.text: every function associate imports today exists under the documented name and returns the same result on the saved test exports

claims.instruction: Source: associate/accuracy at associate main 266dad3. Do not import associate from evidence-cli.

claims.text: the checker's settings (source kinds, the reason-to-check mapping, the minimum quote length) are an explicit input; the command accepts a settings file and otherwise uses a bundled default that it names in its output

honesty_conditions.text: running evidence check with no settings file prints which default settings it used and their version

claims.text: evidence check reports, per run and summed, the counts by kind and by source kind, and lists each place its own re-check disagrees with the counts the harness wrote; a run with no facts is reported as not applicable, not as zero

honesty_conditions.text: on a fixture whose report.json was edited to a wrong count, the command names that count as a disagreement

claims.text: reviewer flags are written to a file beside the run, in a location the run did not write, and no file of the export is modified or created inside it

honesty_conditions.text: a checksum of every file under the export directory is unchanged after the command

claims.text: evidence grade takes the answer text as an explicit input, with the task's expected values, and returns matches, does not match or cannot tell, with the expected items found and missing; it never reads the facts list to decide, and calls no model

honesty_conditions.text: the result is unchanged when the export's facts.json is absent, and a grade is reproduced exactly on a second run

claims.text: expected values are data with a schema and a version: items that must appear, items that must not, and alternatives, compared after the same normalisation the matcher uses; a result names the schema version it was graded under

honesty_conditions.text: two results are reported as comparable only when their schema versions are equal, and a task file with an unknown key is refused

claims.text: the words printed keep the two results apart: the run check is described as counts of checked quotes and backed conclusions, the answer check as a match against recorded expected values, and neither as quality, correctness of the work, or accuracy; each output carries the line that a complete trail does not mean the work is correct

honesty_conditions.text: a test fails if either command's output contains the words quality score or accuracy

claims.text: the shared test vectors ship inside the evidence-cli package, so associate can compare its own copy with the installed one

honesty_conditions.text: associate's copy and the packaged copy are compared by a test in associate and are equal at the pinned versions

claims.text: CLAUDE.md is re-initialised from its seed into a real project file that states the two results, the public library names and the no-dependency rule

honesty_conditions.text: the file no longer contains the seed's re-init instruction

claims.text: no runtime dependency, no model call and no network access; the same inputs give the same output

honesty_conditions.text: the package's dependencies list is empty and no module imports a network library

claims.text: evidence-cli never imports associate, and never edits a run; the TypeScript checker stays in associate's extension

honesty_conditions.text: no file under evidence/ imports associate, and the fixture checksums are unchanged by the test suite

scope_entries.surface: evidence-cli tree at origin/main (git ls-files evidence tests, pyproject.toml, CLAUDE.md)
scope_entries.finding: The package is the template scaffold: evidence/cli/_commands holds cli, doctor, explain, learn, overview, whoami and nothing else; tests are test_cli.py and test_cli_introspection.py; version 0.6.1; dependencies = [] (pyproject.toml:16); requires Python 3.12 or newer; CLAUDE.md is a seed placeholder that says to re-initialise it.

The brief's load-bearing distinction: a high evidence grade means the trail is complete and traceable, not that the work is correct; the lane is the trail around the code, never the code's correctness. It asks for a rubric that is data with a version, sub-scores that cite the artifact that justified them, a not-applicable outcome distinct from missing, and determinism or disclosed non-determinism. It names storybook-cli as an overlap to settle.

Asks to read one export or many and report counts per run and summed; re-run the quote match from the saved files and report disagreements with the harness's counts; write reviewer flags to a file beside the result; stay read-only on the run. Acceptance: counts equal a hand count on a fixture, identical report on re-run, hand-back byte-identical, and the report named for what it is.

scope_entries.surface: associate/accuracy/ at associate main 266dad3 (matcher.py, check.py, counts.py, 1,079 lines) and its importers
scope_entries.finding: Public functions: check_quote (matcher.py:56), parse_source_ref, check_handback, load_export, load_handback_input, inspect_export, accuracy_result (check.py:69,550,666,763,811,883), fact_counts (counts.py:32). check_handback takes the accuracy settings as an argument (check.py:7, 550) and reads no associate file. Importers in associate: harness/pi.py:88, harness/stub.py:21, cli/_commands/check.py:15-16, and six test files. The code is standard library only (check.py:5).
